name: Fashionmogging

card.summary: Fashionmogging means out-dressing another person so that your clothing and style make you look better than they do in the same setting.
card.note: A community term for comparative style; related to stylemaxxing and drip culture.

quick.overview:
Fashionmogging is the use of clothing and styling to look better than someone else, 'mogging' being forum slang for visibly outclassing another person. It extends the looksmaxxing idea of comparing facial or physical features to the realm of dress.

Clothing changes how a body and face are perceived: fit, colour, material and silhouette all affect the impression a person makes. Fashion scholars note that people are judged by what they wear, so style is one of the more changeable parts of appearance.
quick.how: In practice people work on fit, colour choices, grooming-matched outfits and accessories, and compare themselves with others at gatherings or in photos. It is usually discussed alongside stylemaxxing and dripmaxxing rather than as a separate method.
quick.risks: There are no physical risks. Costs can rise if people buy expensive clothing, and the comparative framing can be competitive; replica and budget approaches are discussed in related entries.

lead: Fashionmogging is a looksmaxxing-culture term for dressing more stylishly than another person, so that the outfit shifts a side-by-side comparison in your favour. 'Mogging' in these communities means outshining someone in looks or presence, and fashionmogging applies that to clothing.

Style is one of the most adjustable parts of appearance. Fashion scholars describe clothing, footwear, accessories and grooming as combining into outfits that signal status, self-expression and group belonging, and the same garment can look different depending on the wearer's body and whether it is new, worn or tailored.[1] Susan B. Kaiser, cited in the same overview, argues that people are inevitably judged by what they wear.[1]
No study has measured 'fashionmogging' as such. It overlaps with the wiki's entries on stylemaxxing and dripmaxxing, which cover the broader practice of improving looks through clothing.

chain: Looks more appealing than the comparison person
angle.text: Clothing changes silhouette, colour contrast and perceived polish, so people use it to look better in side-by-side situations. It can be done without changing the face or body.

paras: The term is a compound of 'fashion' and 'mog'. It describes a comparative contest in dress rather than a fixed method.
Fashion in the broad sense includes footwear, accessories, cosmetics and jewellery combined into outfits that signal personality, status and belonging.[1]

Fashion scholarship notes that evaluation of a person depends on colour, material, silhouette and how a garment sits on the body.[1] That supports the general premise that clothing influences impressions, though no research addresses fashionmogging by name.
The term circulates as slang rather than as a codified protocol, and is closely related to the entries on stylemaxxing, dripmaxxing and fit-check culture.
